howDoI.q: How do I make a wall my hero can walk through?
How do I make a wall that looks just like a secret one but stops her?
How do I make a block that turns into one block, and then another?
How do I show a wall cracking before it falls?
How do I hint at a secret without giving it away?
How do I keep a secret room from being found from above?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Looks Like a Wall is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Walk into a wall to see what it does. Nothing in this game can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: Same Look
pages.html:
Level 1: Same Look

A WALL AND A PICTURE OF A WALL CAN LOOK THE SAME comes first. THIS WALL IS REAL. JUMP OVER IT stands before a brick wall two blocks high: walk into it and it stops you, so jump over. THIS ONE IS ONLY A PICTURE. WALK IN stands before a taller wall, four blocks high, drawn exactly the same. Walk into it and you go straight through. SOLID IS A BLOCK SETTING, NOT A LOOK comes last, before three coins and the door.

There are two coins over the first wall, and three past the second.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The real wall. Open sd.bbl in the blocks editor and pick wall. Its Solid boxes are all checked, so Mia cannot walk through it from any side.
  • The picture of a wall. Pick fake. Its picture is the same brick as wall, pixel for pixel, but none of its Solid boxes are checked. Mia walks into it and through it. Whether a block is solid is a setting of the block, and the picture has no say in it.
  • Why the picture is tall. Mia can jump a little over three blocks. A wall four blocks high cannot be jumped, so the only way on is through it. The signs say so, so this is not a trick.
  • The map. Open one.map in the map editor. The real wall is two cells of wall and the picture is four cells of fake. The Level check lists blocks that look alike but act differently, and it finds these two. It cannot know you meant it, so that finding is only a suggestion.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door at the end to the next level in sd.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: Bump, Then Bump
pages.html:
Level 2: Bump, Then Bump

BUMP IT AND IT CRACKS stands before a wall four blocks high. Walk into it: the two bricks at Mia's height become a cracked brick you can walk into, and then a pile of chips. The two above her head stay as an arch. THE CRACK IS A BLOCK TOO. TOUCH IT AGAIN comes next. EACH BLOCK CHANGES ON ITS OWN comes before a wall two bricks thick: each column takes its own touch.

There are nine coins, ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The wall. Open sd.bbl and pick loose. It looks like wall and is solid. On its Touch tab, Becomes block is cracked.
  • The crack. Pick cracked. It is the brick with a crack across it and it is not solid, so Mia walks into it. Its Becomes block is chips. That is a chain: one touch makes the next block, and touching that makes the one after.
  • The chips. Pick chips. It has nothing to turn into, so the chain ends here.
  • Each link needs a touch. Mia presses on a solid wall for a moment, which is a touch, and that changes the block. Then she walks into the cracked block, which is the second touch. A chain does not wait: each link changes as soon as Mia touches that block.
  • Only what you touch changes. Mia is two blocks tall, so she touches two blocks of the wall. The ones above her head are never touched. Open two.map in the map editor and look at the arch.
  • The signs and the exit. A scene link joins the door to the next level in sd.gam.

pages.head: Level 3: Coins in the Wall
pages.html:
Level 3: Coins in the Wall

COINS SHOWING IN A WALL? WALK IN comes first, then A FAIR SECRET GETS A HINT. Further on is a low wall of brick with four coins showing in it. Walk into it and the coins are yours. A roof of real brick runs along its top, so you can also jump on it.

The four coins are worth forty points. Nothing else in the level depends on the wall: a secret is a bonus, and the way to the door is never hidden.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The wall. Open three.map in the map editor. The roof is a row of wall cells. Under it are two rows of fake cells, the picture of a wall, with a coin in four of them.
  • The hint. A coin has a picture with open air around it, so each one shows as a coin in a window. A player who sees a coin where a wall should be knows to try it. That is a fair secret.
  • The roof. The roof is real, so the fake bricks under it stay a pocket in a wall and not just a row of bricks standing in the open.
  • The exit. The last door links to the The End scene in sd.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot hide from the Level check. The check lists a block you can walk through that looks like one you cannot. It cannot tell a secret you meant from a mistake, so say so in your own notes and ignore the finding if it is fair.
  • It cannot tell which side was hit. A fake wall is open from every side, and a real one is closed from every side. There is no wall you can only walk through from the left.
  • A touch cannot wait. A block becomes its next block as soon as it is touched. A chain does not give you a pause between links. For a delay, use a block's timer, which every copy of that block shares.
  • A block changes only itself. Touching one wall block cannot open the wall next to it.
  • A wall that is a picture cannot be told from a real one by looking. Only the signs and the coins say which is which, so plan the hints.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Tick every Solid box on fake and walk into the wall again.
  • Redraw fake a little darker so players can tell it from wall.
  • Add a second crack between cracked and chips and bump the wall again.
  • Make a fake floor and let Mia fall through it.
  • Put a coin in a wall of your own as a hint.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
